blockers.quote: A paper snap above your own head, out of frame. His grin stops. His eyes go up, and read something. We never see the number.
blockers.why: Fails “No new power rule after the halfway point.” Min-jun seeing your tag reverses the established rule that nobody sees the tags but you.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “A paper snap above your own head, out of frame. Min-jun’s grin stops at your face—not the air above it. You look up, unable to see your own card. We never see the number.”

suggestions.quote: You stand on the academy steps. And you say it. Into the crowd.
suggestions.fix: Replace with “So you climb the academy steps and say it into the crowd,” making the experiment a therefore beat.

suggestions.quote: Across eleven studies, the most common regret of a life is education, about a third of all regrets (c11).
suggestions.fix: Move this before line 304 so Ji-yoon’s abandoned education sharpens the dilemma before you choose the bus.

suggestions.quote: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver (c08). Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing (c08).
suggestions.fix: Cut this from the peak and move directly from her old letter to what her number means; the comparison interrupts the emotional turn.

keep.quote: A tag has one colour for every kind of hurt.
She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
That half-second is the other life, going past.
